ensemble_topup.on: the 18 graphs whose optimality SCIP did not certify
ensemble_topup.purpose: test whether the 30 s reference R_i is converged; a 10x budget that fails to beat R_i is evidence that R_i is at or very near the optimum, which is exactly the unresolved case the certification pass left open
ensemble_topup.separate_outdir: logs_topup (the primary 30 s records in logs/ are never overwritten, so the two budget regimes stay distinguishable)

upper_bounds.purpose: a rigorous U_i for every graph, so that an uncertified R_i is still bracketed rather than open-ended

question_answered: which graph had which budget applied, and where any budget was reduced relative to the headline

reductions.history: An earlier window did not finish in time; nothing was reduced then either -- the 1800 primary run records already on disk are the full sweep, and the resume only had to assemble them.
reductions.statement: No budget was reduced relative to the headline, and no graph was dropped. All 60 graphs (48 dev+eval as required, plus the 12 calibration graphs) received the full ensemble budget of 6 heuristics x 5 seeds x 30 s = 30 runs, plus a 120 s SCIP attempt, plus the upper-bound computation. The 18 uncertified graphs additionally received 6 runs of 300 s each.
